title: Ranking and Tier Structure
description: Preserves complete reconstructable order, tiers, evaluation criteria, price ranges and host differences.
principles: Reconstruct the complete safely supported order or tier structure.
Mark uncertain order rather than inventing precision.
Every ranked subject needs enough explanation to preserve placement, positive case and risk when discussed.
Keep source board, market order and format-specific order distinct.

dimensions.description: Complete rank, tier or board structure.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve every safely reconstructable subject and break.
detection_questions: Is order or tier membership uncertain?

dimensions.description: Criteria used to create the ranking.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain explicit criteria and weighting language.
detection_questions: What drives the order: talent, role, price, format or scarcity?

dimensions.description: Reason each subject occupies its place.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the key positive and negative placement reasons.
detection_questions: Why is this subject above or below adjacent options?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Explain the break and downstream draft implication.

dimensions.description: Rookie picks, rounds, ADP or trade ranges.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve exact or approximate ranges and price sensitivity.
detection_questions: At what range does value change?

dimensions.description: Difference between source ranking and expected market.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Keep talent/conviction and market behavior separate.
detection_questions: Does need or scarcity move subjects above the source's pure board?

dimensions.description: Changes by scoring or league format.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve alternate ordering or specialist value.
detection_questions: Does the ranking change by format?

passing: Preserve the reference only where it is needed to understand another argument.
Do not create an artificial standalone evaluation.
brief: Preserve the conclusion and its immediate qualifier or condition.
Do not expand beyond what the source supports.
substantive: Preserve the conclusion plus the meaningful reason, condition, risk or uncertainty supplied by the source.
Keep format, price or time-horizon distinctions when they materially change the view.
deep: Preserve the complete major reasoning chain rather than only the final verdict.
Represent every materially discussed dimension, including competing positive and negative cases.
Keep disagreements, uncertainty, conditions and failure paths.
structural: Preserve the broad thesis, its mechanism, its scope and the subjects it affects.
Create independently reusable context takes rather than burying the thesis inside one player.

review_questions: Can the complete source ranking or tier structure be reconstructed?
Does every important subject have enough rationale for its placement?
Are tier breaks, price ranges and direct comparisons retained?
Are market order and source preference clearly distinguished?
forbidden_distortions: Do not invent exact ranks from unordered discussion.
Do not omit lower-ranked subjects because conviction is low.
Do not reduce each player to a one-line verdict when the source gives a deep profile.
Do not merge host rankings without recording disagreement.
extension_signals: A new ranking format or board structure appears.
The source uses a recurring tie-breaker not represented.
A ranking episode would be a useful reference case.
